lines.text: Evil eye beads have their own village.
A village near Izmir was renamed Nazarkoy, meaning evil eye village.
lines.say: A village near IZ-meer was renamed nah-ZAHR-kuh-ee, meaning evil eye village.

lines.text: It earned that name because its workshops make so many beads.
Makers pull molten glass on iron rods and shape it by hand.
Makers have melted green wine bottles to make green beads.
Beads also come shaped like walnuts and eggs.
Around the Mediterranean, glass eye beads date back about 2,500 years.

post.caption: Evil eye beads have their own village. A village near Izmir was renamed Nazarkoy, meaning evil eye village. It earned that name because its workshops make so many beads. Makers pull molten glass on iron rods and shape it by hand. Makers have melted green wine bottles to make green beads. Beads also come shaped like walnuts and eggs. Around the Mediterranean, glass eye beads date back about 2,500 years. In Greece the charm is called the mati, meaning eye. Many say a cracked bead has soaked up an envious look. In Cappadocia, whole trees are hung with nazar charms. The nazar amulet became an emoji in 2018.
